findings.problem: AC-6 requires the reopened window to be raised to the front, but the test opened only one window, so the raise clause was unfalsifiable.
findings.resolution: Second window opened first; the assertion now compares the two modeless layers' computed z-index before and after the reopen.

findings.problem: AC-3 asserted the read's sessionId and the docked geometry but never the window's tab binding, which a bug binding to activeTabId would survive.
findings.resolution: A second tab is created; the window is asserted to hide when that tab is active and to return on switching back, with the mounted count held at one.

findings.problem: AC-1 and AC-2 pinned the item order, which the AC states as a set.
findings.resolution: Membership compared as a sorted set; the count is asserted separately.

findings.problem: afterEach had no project guard, so on Mobile Safari and Tablet it would touch a page that never navigated and time out for 15s per test.
findings.resolution: Guarded with the same project check as beforeEach.

findings.problem: Cleanup had no error containment, so one teardown failure would leak a tab and a window into the next test's counts.
findings.resolution: Teardown wrapped; routes are also unrouted.

findings.problem: removeOwnTabs matched by name prefix only while deleting against one workspace id.
findings.resolution: Filter scoped by workspace id as well.

findings.problem: Absence-of-request assertions read a snapshot taken the instant a DOM assertion resolved.
findings.resolution: A settle delay precedes each absence claim, and the traffic filters now match on the resolved path rather than on totals.

findings.problem: AC-7 read the server-persisted activeTabId once, racing the persistence.

req-mapping.result: test_case ids, req_id and ac_refs match the sidecar task; the seven test titles equal the seven test_symbol values

gate.note: both HIGH findings from each axis resolved in iteration 2 of the draft
